mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, indicating supply chain disruptions, will lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as companies struggle to meet demand and earnings estimates are revised downward.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of months following a 1%+ m/m drop in IP.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected spike in the unemployment rate, signaling a rapidly weakening labor market, will trigger a risk-off sentiment and produce negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day SPX returns are positive in > 40% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, indicating a restrictive monetary policy, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 20 trading days as the higher cost of capital weighs on equity valuations.
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are positive in > 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts and retail sales both decline by more than 5% year-over-year, signaling a broad-based weakening of consumer demand, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 40% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS are down > 5% y/y.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate is below 4% and payroll employment growth accelerates by more than 200k jobs m/m, signaling a dangerously overheating labor market, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 20 trading days as the Fed is forced to tighten policy aggressively.
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are positive in > 60% of periods when UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS growth > 200k m/m.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPI is rising by more than 3% year-over-year and the federal funds rate is below 2%, signaling that monetary policy is too loose for the level of inflation, S&P 500 returns will be negative over the next 60 trading days as the market anticipates a hawkish policy pivot.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive in > 50% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3% y/y and FEDFUNDS < 2%.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production is growing by more than 5% year-over-year and the ISM manufacturing PMI is above 60, signaling a red-hot industrial sector, S&P 500 returns will be positive over the next 20 trading days as strong manufacturing activity boosts economic growth.
failure_condition: 20-day SPX returns are negative in > 40% of periods when INDPRO growth > 5% y/y and ISM manufacturing PMI > 60.
